samples.text:
The pie charts illustrates the proportion of energy which was used for different purposes in a typical home in one country in 1990 and in 2020.

In 1990, space heating was the biggest use of energy, it made up 58% of the total. Water heating was in second place with 22%. The other three categories was quite small, cooking was 7%, appliances accounted for 8% and lighting only 5%.

In 2020, space heating was still the largest part but it decreased to 44%. Also, water heating dropped to 18%. Cooking and lighting also went down a little, to 6% and 3% respectively. However, the appliances had a big increase, from 8% to 29%, so this became the second biggest category in 2020 and it was more than water heating. This was the only use of energy that increased in the period.

Overall, heating the space used the most of energy in both years, but the share of appliances grow a lot and all the other uses become smaller than before.
samples.why: Covers all categories with accurate figures · overview is basic and placed at the end · mechanical linking (Also, However) · adequate vocabulary · several agreement, article and tense errors.

samples.text:
The two pie charts compare the ways in which energy was consumed in an average household in a particular country in 1990 and 2020.

Overall, space heating remained the main use of household energy in both years, although its share declined noticeably. The most striking change was the dramatic rise in the proportion used by appliances, while every other category fell slightly.

In 1990, more than half of domestic energy (58%) went on heating rooms, and water heating accounted for a further 22%. By contrast, appliances, cooking and lighting each represented less than a tenth of the total, at 8%, 7% and 5% respectively, so together they made up only a fifth of consumption.

Thirty years later, the figure for space heating had dropped to 44%, and water heating had also decreased, to 18%. Cooking and lighting saw only marginal falls, to 6% and 3%. Appliances, on the other hand, grew from 8% to 29%, which means their share more than tripled and they overtook water heating to become the second largest use of energy in the home.
samples.why: Clear overview of main trends · key changes well highlighted with accurate figures · logical progression with a range of linkers · some less common vocabulary · mostly error-free sentences.

samples.text:
The pie charts show how energy consumption in a typical home in one country was divided between five uses in 1990 and 2020.

It is clear that heating living space consumed the largest share of household energy in both years, although its dominance weakened over the period. Meanwhile, appliances rose from a minor category to the second largest, at the expense of every other use.

In 1990, space heating alone absorbed 58% of the energy used in the home, and together with water heating (22%) it accounted for four-fifths of the total. The remaining three uses were comparatively insignificant: appliances took 8%, cooking 7% and lighting a mere 5%.

By 2020, this pattern had shifted considerably. The share devoted to space heating had contracted to 44%, and water heating had slipped to 18%, so the two combined now made up just 62%. Cooking and lighting also edged down, to 6% and 3% respectively. In sharp contrast, the proportion consumed by appliances more than tripled to 29%, overtaking water heating and becoming the only category to expand over the thirty-year period.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected · clear, well-placed overview · figures used selectively for comparison · cohesion managed smoothly · precise vocabulary (absorbed, contracted, edged down) · wide range of error-free structures.
